title: Singleton generator for the first constant residue kernel
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and X a Noetherian scheme in universe u. Let O and q be the small constant section ring and first residue map [def-sfb-internal-completion-section-transport]. There exists a global section a of O whose singleton list generates the module of the ideal kernelIdeal(q), with the prescribed inclusion, on every slice [def-weil-pbc-ringed-ideal-generators]. This is an underived ideal calculation and asserts nothing about derived completeness.

source.place: Proof (1), completion comparison; constant-coefficient criterion (2)--(3); Stacks 099I, 099L, 099M

proof.text: Apply the discrete quotient coefficient comparison to the valuation ring and its first uniformizer ideal. Its image under ULift is the principal ideal generated by the lifted uniformizer.

The constant coefficient kernel formula at level one says the kernel is the principal ideal of the constant uniformizer section. Evaluate the commuting comparison square on each object. The source and target comparison maps are bijective, so the actual kernel is the ideal-map image of that principal ideal, hence is principal with generator the transported global section.

On each slice, restrict the resulting global section. Apply ideal_generated_global_sections to the restricted ideal and this singleton list, using the sectionwise principal-ideal equality. Evaluate its inclusion equality at the terminal slice object. This is exactly IsRingedIdealGeneratingList.

proof_origin.place: Proof (1): constant kernel formula transported across the coefficient quotient square, followed by singleton generation on each slice

lean.statement:
theorem residue_generator [IsNoetherian X] :
    ∃ a : ((ring l E X).obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections,
      ∀ U : Scheme.coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, u} X,
        IsRingedIdealGeneratingList (ring l E X)
          (ConstantCompletion.kernelIdeal (residue l E X)).module
          (ConstantCompletion.kernelIdeal (residue l E X)).inclusion U 1
          (fun _ ↦ a.val (op U))
